title: Kidney imaging and biopsy

steps.tx: **Renal ultrasound** demonstrates normal bipolar renal length of 10 to 12 cm with cortical echogenicity normally equal to or less than adjacent liver parenchyma, while increased echogenicity signifies medical renal parenchymal disease. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Renal **resistive index** (RI) measured by spectral Doppler ultrasound is calculated as (peak systolic velocity - end diastolic velocity) / peak systolic velocity, where values exceeding 0.70 indicate elevated intrarenal vascular impedance. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Technetium-99m **DMSA** (dimercaptosuccinic acid) binds to proximal tubular cells and provides cortical imaging to detect renal scarring, while Tc-99m MAG3 is cleared by tubular secretion, optimal for dynamic renography in obstruction. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice, reflecting renogram.

steps.tx: **Gadolinium**-based contrast agents in patients with severe kidney disease (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2 or on dialysis) carry a risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF), highest with linear non-ionic chelate formulations. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Absolute contraindications to **percutaneous native kidney biopsy** include uncorrected bleeding diathesis, severe refractory hypertension, solitary functioning native kidney (relative), and active renal or perinephric infection. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: A diagnostically adequate percutaneous **renal biopsy** specimen requires at least 8 to 10 glomeruli for light microscopy and at least 1 to 2 glomeruli each for immunofluorescence and electron microscopy examination. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: Post-biopsy **arteriovenous fistula**s develop in up to 10% of cases, diagnosed by high-velocity low-resistance turbulent jet on color Doppler, with the vast majority resolving spontaneously within 1 to 2 years. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.

steps.tx: **Electron microscopy** in renal biopsy is mandatory for evaluating glomerular basement membrane thickness, podocyte foot process effacement in minimal change disease, and ultrastructural subendothelial or subepithelial deposits. This established clinical parameter guides diagnostic evaluation, risk stratification, and evidence-based therapeutic management in specialized nephrology practice.
